$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=2x+y-z,\, & y(0)=1 \\ {z}^{′}=x+2y+z,\, & z(0)=2\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Δy={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ Δz={z}^{′}\cdot Δx\end{aligned}
$$

With this in mind, let's approximate the values of $y(1)$ and $z(1)$ for our initial value problem above using Euler's method with step size $\Delta x = 1.$

We start by constructing a table that contains all relevant quantities, including slopes and increments for *both* variables.
Then, because the initial conditions are $y(0)=1$ and $z(0)=2,$ we place $x=0,$ $y=1,$ and $z=2$ in the first row.

| $x$ | $y$ | $y'$ | $\Delta y$ | $z$ | $z'$ | $\Delta z$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ |  |  | $2$ |  |  |

Next, we compute *both $y'$ and $z'$* according to the given rules using the current values of $x,$ $y,$ and $z{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2x+y-z\, & \,{z}^{′} & =x+2y+z \\  & =2\cdot 0+1-2 &  & =0+2\cdot 1+2 \\  & =-1 &  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | $y'$ | $\Delta y$ | $z$ | $z'$ | $\Delta z$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-1$ |  | $2$ | $4$ |  |

Finally, we compute $\Delta y$ and $\Delta z$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx\, & \,Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(-1)\cdot 1 &  & =4\cdot 1 \\  & =-1 &  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | $y'$ | $\Delta y$ | $z$ | $z'$ | $\Delta z$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $4$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ in the *next* row, we add $\Delta x$ to $x,$ $\Delta y$ to $y,$ and $\Delta z$ to $z,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=0+1=1 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=1+(-1)=0 \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=2+4=6\end{aligned}

| $x$ | $y$ | $y'$ | $\Delta y$ | $z$ | $z'$ | $\Delta z$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Notice that this component-wise approach is not specific to Euler's method. Indeed, we could apply any numerical method component-wise to approximate the solution to a system of ODEs!

tutorials.name: Euler's Method for Larger Systems of ODEs
tutorials.problem:
We can apply Euler's method to a system of *any number* of simultaneous first-order ODEs. That is, for an initial value problem

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{′}={f}_{1}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{1}(a)={c}_{1}, \\ {y}_{2}^{′}={f}_{2}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{2}(a)={c}_{2}, \\ \,\,⋮ \\ {y}_{m}^{′}={f}_{m}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{m}(a)={c}_{m},\end{aligned}
$$

Euler's method approximates a solution by applying the update rule component-wise. The increments are

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{1}={y}_{1}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ Δ{y}_{2}={y}_{2}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ \,\,\,⋮ \\ Δ{y}_{m}={y}_{m}^{′}\cdot Δx\end{aligned}
$$

The new values are then given by $y_{i,\text{new}} = y_i + \Delta y_i,$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,m.$

For convenience, we can express large systems of ODEs in vector form. Let

Then, the initial value problem

$$
\mathbf{y}' = \mathbf{f}(x, \mathbf{y}), \qquad \mathbf{y}(a) = \mathbf{c},
$$

has Euler update

$$
\Delta \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{y}' \cdot \Delta x
\qquad
\mathbf{y}_\text{new} = \mathbf{y} + \Delta \mathbf{y}.
$$

Next, we will apply this vector formulation to a specific numerical example.

tutorials.title: Euler's Method for Larger Systems of ODEs
tutorials.content:
We can apply Euler's method to a system of *any number* of simultaneous first-order ODEs. That is, for an initial value problem

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{′}={f}_{1}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{1}(a)={c}_{1}, \\ {y}_{2}^{′}={f}_{2}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{2}(a)={c}_{2}, \\ \,\,⋮ \\ {y}_{m}^{′}={f}_{m}(x,{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{m}),\, & {y}_{m}(a)={c}_{m},\end{aligned}
$$

Euler's method approximates a solution by applying the update rule component-wise. The increments are

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{1}={y}_{1}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ Δ{y}_{2}={y}_{2}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ \,\,\,⋮ \\ Δ{y}_{m}={y}_{m}^{′}\cdot Δx\end{aligned}
$$

The new values are then given by $y_{i,\text{new}} = y_i + \Delta y_i,$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,m.$

For convenience, we can express large systems of ODEs in vector form. Let
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274617/assets/2c08a3c473755170afa7ad645479e90107d354f1bfd1c917ca1bfaaeaeaad9d7.svg)

Then, the initial value problem

$$
\mathbf{y}' = \mathbf{f}(x, \mathbf{y}), \qquad \mathbf{y}(a) = \mathbf{c},
$$

has Euler update

$$
\Delta \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{y}' \cdot \Delta x
\qquad
\mathbf{y}_\text{new} = \mathbf{y} + \Delta \mathbf{y}.
$$

Next, we will apply this vector formulation to a specific numerical example.
